toolsetModuleName: Meshy2Aurora TLC Guard Longsword item v7
areaName: TLC Guard Longsword Item Properties V7
observations: The exact V7 custom 2/6/2 Item is visible and internally connected in Item Properties, and its icon has the accepted upright order.
Replacing custom Bottom 2 with native Bottom 3 leaves the native hilt detached below the custom Middle/Top assembly.
Replacing custom Middle 6 with native Middle 7 leaves the custom Top detached above the native Bottom/Middle assembly.
The all-native 3/7/3 comparison assembles coherently in one shared Item-local coordinate frame.
In NWN the exact V7 equipped sword is visible but displaced relative to the character hand; the Item origin does not coincide with the native longsword grip region.
Blade length is not the reported defect. The rejected criterion is the slot-local scale and translation of Bottom, Middle and Top and the resulting equipped grip offset.

diagnosedCause.summary: The current fitter creates a new sequential bounding-box chain at Item-local Y=0 instead of fitting every generated part into the retail BaseItem/ItemClass slot frame. Aurora appends the part MDLs without inventing slot offsets, and equipped rendering attaches the shared Item-local origin to the character hand. The custom origin is at the lower end of the pommel assembly rather than inside the native WSwLs grip frame.
diagnosedCause.baseitemsBoundary: baseitems.2da selects ModelType, ItemClass and equipability but contains no XYZ grip or per-part translation columns. The spatial contract is authored in each MDL node controller and is interpreted relative to the creature hand attachment; creature appearance may additionally apply WEAPONSCALE.

minimalNextArtifactDelta: Replace the WSwLs sequential target-length/cursor fitter with a retail-reference-derived shared Item-local slot-frame profile.

Fit and bake each Meshy Bottom, Middle and Top independently into its corresponding native slot envelope while preserving the common Item origin; do not recenter the first part to Y=0 and do not stack later parts from a bounding-box cursor.
Bind the frame profile to the effective BaseItem, ItemClass, ModelType and attachment route, with in-place retail reader provenance and numeric invariant readback.
Add mixed native/custom slot-frame conformance tests and a distinct equipped-render witness using the same real UTI; a ground Item-only fixture cannot close grip acceptance.
Keep CAPART robes/body parts and cloaks on their own skeleton/body-node attachment profiles rather than reusing the weapon-hand frame.
